summary: Discovery focused on pricing/unit economics: per-token pricing, batching and KV caching levers, and customer budget constraints. Pacific wants to compare hosted vs Dedicated vs Private options; prioritized cost predictability and data isolation. Agreed to run benchmarks and a cost model worksheet.
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-03-30 16:00 PDT
Duration: 48 minutes
Attendees: Jenna Park (Redwood AE), Marcus Li (Redwood SE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE); Ravi Kapoor (CTO), Elena Santos (ML Eng), Maya Chen (Infra), Samir Patel (Product)

[00:00] Jenna Park: hey everyone, thanks for joining, excited to talk through cost and unit economics, quick intro from our side - i'm jenna, i'll run the commercial convo, marcus and priya will do the technical parts
[00:12] Ravi Kapoor: great, thanks jenna. quick context: we're Pacific Analytics, building realtime insights for maritime logistics, heavy streaming ingestion, a mix of short prompts and longer summarization. current infra is GCP, some on-prem for sensitive clients. main question is when does hosted make sense vs dedicated or private. our monthly budget for inference is roughly $20k to start, could go up if unit costs improve
[00:34] Marcus Li: cool, thanks ravi. couple threads we'll cover: per-token pricing assumptions for hosted, how dedicated reserved capacity changes unit economics, and levers like batching, KV prefix caching and quantization. also practical throughput numbers and what we typically see for latency impact
[00:55] Elena Santos: can you clarify per-token? is that input+output tokens? and do you charge for cache hits?
[01:05] Jenna Park: good q. hosted per-token pricing is on a input+output basis, yes. cache hits still count compute but we have prefix/KV caching that can drop compute per-request; the hosted pricing model discounts for heavy cache/batching scenarios via lower effective tokens on the invoice when we can short-circuit generation - i'll send the exact line items in the pricing sheet
[01:28] Maya Chen: when you say short-circuit, is that something on our network or on your side? data residency is a must for some clients
[01:36] Priya Nair: for hosted it's in our cloud and caching happens in memory in the serving tier; for private or dedicated you can enable customer-local KV cache so the cache stays in your VPC/on-prem. there's a nuance where a cache hit avoids autoregressive decoding work which drastically lowers GPU time
[01:52] Samir Patel: so, rough order: with dedicated reserved, what's per-token cost vs hosted? like 30% cheaper? 50%?
[02:00] Marcus Li: it depends on throughput and model family. ballpark for a medium Llama-like open model: hosted might be $0.0008 - $0.002 per token depending on model; dedicated with reserved capacity and high sustained throughput often drops effective unit cost 30-60% because of amortized GPU utilization, batching, and longer sequence/kernel optimizations. again those numbers are illustrative, we'll run your workload through our cost worksheet
[02:28] Elena Santos: how does batching change things? our requests are bursty - many small prompts, some long contexts
[02:35] Marcus Li: batching helps a ton for small prompts; continuous batching in our runtime groups concurrent requests to increase GPU amortization. for latency-sensitive short prompts we still preserve tail latency SLOs by adaptive batching; best-case you can see 2-5x cost reduction for tiny 16-64 token prompts when batching is effective. for long contexts, caching (prefix/KV) reduces repeated decode steps so if you have repeated prefixes (like standard system prompts) you avoid recomputing that state
[03:05] Ravi Kapoor: are there any changes to output quality when quantizing to reduce cost? we have some regulatory clients and can't lose accuracy on certain predictions
[03:14] Priya Nair: quantization can introduce small quality regressions; our Optimize team has model-specific recommendations and we ship quant profiles tested for minimal quality loss. we recommend running A/B evals on your prompt set as part of the PoC; for many workloads int8 quant yields 1-3% delta on evaluated metrics but big wins on throughput and memory
[03:38] Maya Chen: what's the onboarding for Dedicated trial? we have subnet/VPC restrictions, private key management and need audit logs
[03:45] Jenna Park: Dedicated trial is usually a 2-4 week reserved instance, we provision a tenant with reserved GPU pool. for VPC peering or private deployments we support customer-managed networking, KMS integration, and audit logs. we'll share SOC2 and the network runbook
[03:58] Samir Patel: our finance team wants examples: for $20k/month what can we expect in tokens? any sample scenarios?
[04:06] Marcus Li: quick sketch: if you're doing mostly short prompts (~32 input + 32 output tokens average = 64 tokens total) and you get good batching, at $0.0008/token effective you'd get ~25M tokens. with dedicated and good batching maybe $0.0004/token effective -> 50M tokens. but if you have long summaries (1k tokens) that obviously changes the math. we'll plug your telemetry into the cost model and return scenarios
[04:35] Elena Santos: we have a mix: 70% short prompts, 30% long summaries (about 600-1200 tokens). also some clients require retention = zero, so private deployment is on the table
[04:45] Jenna Park: makes sense. for mixed workloads we often recommend a hybrid routing policy: short, latency-sensitive traffic on dedicated or hosted with low-latency SLOs and long batchy jobs on a cheaper quantized variant or even offline job runners. our routing supports automatic fallback when capacity is constrained
[05:05] Ravi Kapoor: curious about billing granularity and credits - if we provision Dedicated but don't fully use it, is there an overage/burst option?
[05:13] Jenna Park: yes, dedicated has reserved commit and we offer burst into shared capacity (hosted) at predictable overage rates. contracts can include a buffer or burst credits. we can model a blended effective cost for planning purposes
[05:25] Maya Chen: latency numbers - what's tail latency for short prompts on dedicated vs hosted? our SLAs are strict for certain features
[05:33] Marcus Li: short prompts on dedicated typically hit p95 ~40-120ms on good GPU hardware (depends on model + sequence length). hosted p95 is comparable for our standard instances but dedicated with pinned capacity reduces jitter. caution: quantization and large batch sizes can increase tail latency; we tune batching windows to meet SLOs
[05:55] Elena Santos: any gotchas with tokenization differences when we move models between hosted and private? we've seen token count swing across tokenizer versions
[06:02] Priya Nair: yes, tokenization differences can change token counts and therefore cost. part of the onboarding we run tokenizer parity checks and account for that in the cost model. we also recommend pinning model versions across environments
[06:18] Samir Patel: security: do you support customer-managed KMS and HSM? we need e2e encryption for certain datasets
[06:25] Jenna Park: yes, for Private and Dedicated we integrate with customer KMS/HSM; hosted supports envelope encryption and we provide keys integration options for enterprise plans. audit logs and RBAC are standard for enterprise customers
[06:38] Ravi Kapoor: ok, so next steps? it sounds like we should run a benchmark and get a detailed cost sheet based on our traces
[06:44] Jenna Park: agreed. proposed next steps: we run a two-week benchmark using a small sample of your traffic, provision a small dedicated pool for the test, run both hosted and dedicated variants, and then produce an itemized cost model and recommendations. we'll also send SOC2 and the pricing sheet.
[06:58] Elena Santos: timeline: we can get sample traces to you by next wednesday. can you give an estimate how long the benchmark setup takes?
[07:06] Marcus Li: provisioning a small dedicated test cluster is usually 48-72 hours, then we run scripts against your samples for 3-5 days to get stable numbers. we'll produce the cost worksheet and quality evals after that
[07:18] Maya Chen: who will own the benchmark on your side?
[07:22] Jenna Park: marcus and priya will run it; jenna will own commercial and contract questions. we'll include a one-pager on network and security requirements
[07:32] Samir Patel: ok great. a couple smaller items: can you share a sample billing CSV for hosted so our finance team can model it quickly?
[07:38] Jenna Park: yes, we'll include a sample billing export and a worked example mapping tokens to dollars at multiple throughput points
[07:45] Ravi Kapoor: any open questions from redwood?
[07:48] Marcus Li: just one: are there any internal constraints around timeline or procurement we should be aware of?
[07:52] Ravi Kapoor: procurement window tends to be 6-8 weeks for anything over $50k annually but we can do faster for pilot spend. the big constraint is data residency for a subset of clients which likely pushes those customers to Private deployments
[08:05] Jenna Park: noted. we'll model a hybrid approach in the deck and show an annualized example and a pilot path under $20k for initial ramp.
[08:15] Elena Santos: thanks, this was helpful.
[08:18] Jenna Park: awesome, i'll capture next steps and send the pricing & security docs today. thanks everyone

Recap & Next steps:
- Redwood to send detailed per-token pricing sheet and sample billing CSV (Jenna)
- Redwood SEs (Marcus + Priya) to provision dedicated trial and run 2-week benchmark with Pacific sample traces (provision 48-72 hrs)
